transcript.text: Amaru is one of the toughest bosses in Dragon Wilds. You can make this boss fight a lot easier though with the
proper strategy and preparation. In this guide, we'll cover everything you need to know to prepare for Amaru. The best
consumables, the right gear to wear, and the rewards this boss provides, including access to the next region in
Runescape Dragon Wilds, Daodan Reach. Hey everyone, it's Bobs. Before I get into this full Amaru boss guide, please
like and hype the video and subscribe if you haven't. We're going to start off by covering who
Amaru is and why it's important to take her down to progress your journey in Dragon Wilds. Keep in mind I still have
timestamps so you can skip ahead to whichever part is most important to you. Amaru is the second main boss in Dragon
Wilds. She's the final boss in the Fel Hollow region and she was once a dragon general like Velgar before she became
undead. You have to beat Amaru to move on to Daodan Reach. If you don't kill this boss, you'll be stuck in Fel Hollow
forever. So, one way or the other, you're going to have to gear up and prepare for taking down this boss if you
want to progress through the game. Amaru is a reasonably tough boss. She has multiple attacks, summons waves of ads,
and has phases where she takes on an ethereal form and you can only damage her if you're soul rifted. Dragon Wilds
veterans generally consider Amaru to be one of the toughest bosses in the game, but again, it's all a matter of which
approach you take, whether you're properly prepared or not. So, speaking of preparation, we have to
talk about how to unlock Amaru in the first place. You can only challenge Amaru after completing the rest of the
main quest in Fel Hollow. Basically, you enter the zone, gather three separate curse fragments, then bring them to her
altar here in Hope's Fall. I do have a full guide on this process that I'm linking both above and the description.
If you have not completed the main quest in Fel Hollow yet, definitely check out that guide because it provides a full
walk through the whole quest, how to get started and collect all three curse fragments. Once you do have all three
fragments, just go to Amaru's Tower at Hope's Fall, interact with the door, and you'll be able to challenge the boss. I
do highly recommend you get properly ready for this fight, though. It'll be quite tough, and having the right
consumables and gear ahead of time is half the battle. So, as far as consumables go, you're
going to want to stack the soul food and sea life buffs. These both provide you with additional health regeneration over
time, and they stack with each other. So, you're going to want one source of soul food and one source of sea life.
The easiest way to get sea life is with sautéed sardines. You unlock this recipe
relatively early in your fishing journey in Dragon Wilds. And to learn more about
how to get sautéed sardines and progress through fishing, check out my full guide to fishing in Dragon Wilds. That's
linked above and the description. When it comes to pumpkin soup, your primary ingredient is going to be roast pumpkin.
Pumpkins grow throughout Fell Hollow, and if you harvest enough, you'll eventually get pumpkin seeds, making it
possible to grow your own pumpkins in a willow farming plot. You can also get the soul food buff with a pumpkin spice
infusion, but doing so will make it impossible to use other infusion buffs. So, I recommend going the pumpkin soup
route instead. As far as your infusion goes, I recommend the evasive infusion because you're going to be doing a lot
of dodging to get out of the way of Amaru's attacks. That does it for food and drinks, but
there are some more consumables we should touch on as well. If you're running a mage build, you're going to
want to use both a magical focus and a lesser magic potion or better. There are corresponding options for both ranged
and melee as well. Whichever item it is for your combat style, you'll want both the item that increases your damage and
your critical chance. I should also mention that when it comes to getting your health back during the fight,
definitely use sautéed sardines and not pumpkin soup. Sautéed sardines have a far lower sustenance value, meaning
they're less likely to make you overeat. Beyond that, that covers it for consumables. Get pumpkin soup, sautéed
sardines, and evasive infusions, plus a damage boosting consumable, and a crit boosting consumable, and you'll be good
to go. Now, let's talk about your gear. I took down Amaru as a mage, so that's what I know about. I would also highly
recommend this approach. Taking down Amaru melee is going to be a lot harder. I'm not sure about ranged, but I know
that using air runes made the process pretty easy. So, to that end, I recommend the necromancer's staff. This
is the best power level five magic weapon you can get. You get it from a very simple puzzle in the dungeon Vek
Chen Venkara that's located here under the waterfall in the Lake of Lost Souls. For more information how to get this
staff, check out my Fell Hollow intro guide, which is linked above in the description. As far as armor goes, I
recommend level five mage armor for the head, whether it's the necromancer's crown or the split bark helm, combined
with a steel plate body and steel plate legs. There's general agreement in the community this is the best approach for
both spell casters and melee fighters. Having two pieces of melee armor and then a magic headpiece. In addition to
that, you're going to want the salve amulet. This gives you 17% damage against the undead, and Amaru is an
undead enemy. The salve amulet gives you a considerably higher boost than the amulet of magic or the corresponding
amulets for melee or ranged against Amaru specifically. I also have a video on how to get the salve amulet that
again is linked above and the description. From there, you should be good to go. Whether you're taking the
magic, melee, or ranged approach, just make sure all your gear is power level five and that you have a salve amulet.
All right, you are now ready to fight Amaru. You can go over to her tower in Hopes Fall and begin the fight. Before
you do though, let's have a quick talk about strategy. Unlike with Velgar where you have to manually summon him, Amaru
will start attacking you the second you enter the middle of the ring. Be prepared for onslaught. She'll start
attacking right off the bat, but if you're using magic, you can fight back. She'll come in and land on the ground,
making herself temporarily vulnerable. From there, she'll just go from side to side of the ring, attacking you from a
distance with her wither orbs. Whatever these are called, the purple glowing orbs she shoots at you, it'll be a
moment until you get to the next damage phase. As you move around the ring, watch out for the withered spots on the
ground. You don't want to become soul rifted until you have to. So, try to keep that eye meter above your stamina
from reaching full. Eventually, Imaru will land again and shoot earth spikes at you. Try to avoid all of her attacks
by dodging, but also keep in mind that your soul food and sea life perks will be regenerating your health relatively
quickly. So, if she does hit you, don't worry about it too much. Eventually, Imaru will use a flamethrower attack on
you. You can either dodge it or go under her belly while she attacks. This is a great opportunity to attack back. During
the fight, Imaru will periodically go back up in the air, go to each corner of the ring, and shoot wither balls at you.
During the early stages of the fight, just avoid these. But, eventually, she'll also summon adds during these
phases that you have to kill before she'll come back down. From this point, it's basically rinse
and repeat, except for Imaru's unique mechanic. At a few points during the fight, she'll turn into a spectral form
and be immune from damage unless you become soul rifted. While she's in this form, she's going to be charging up this
huge attack that actually doesn't do too much damage, but still the idea is that you become withered and damage her to
interrupt this attack. If you hit her enough times while you're soul rifted, she'll stagger on the ground, then just
hit her a couple more times, and she'll go back to normal. At that point, interact with one of the pools of
purification located at the edges of her lair to stop being soul rifted. Imaru will summon adds during these phases,
though, in addition to the spectral enemies that always attack you when you're soul rifted. Plus, you only have
45 seconds to turn Imaru back to normal and purify yourself when you're soul rifted. This is much shorter than the
usual timer when you're soul rifted, so do keep an eye on your time and try to get through this phase as quickly as
possible. That's pretty much all you need to know for this fight. A note about the ads,
though. These are the main danger of the fight. Amaro's attacks themselves are not that powerful. If these guys gang up
on you and attack, though, you'll die pretty quickly. So, always prioritize the ads, and aside from that, just rinse
and repeat. Attack Amaro whenever she's vulnerable, become soul rifted when you have to, try to avoid becoming soul
rifted otherwise, hit her hard and fast when she's in her spectral form, and purify quickly.
At the very end of the fight, Amaro will enter her spectral form one more time. So, become soul rifted again, and do the
final bit of damage you need to do to take her out. Oh, and one thing I forgot to mention is she does periodically do
this pillar of fire thing. That's pretty easy to avoid. And also, toward the end of the fight, she'll kind of fire bomb
you. This attack is very difficult to evade. But yeah, overall, the Amaro fight has a lot going on. It's way more
complex than the Velgar fight. Lots of mechanics to learn. But you really only have to pay attention when there are ads
after you, or when you have to go into soul rifted form with the reduced timer. Otherwise, it's some pretty basic rinse
and repeat stuff that shouldn't be too challenging in the end. And do keep in mind that at the end of the video, I'll
be including the full gameplay of my Amaro takedown that you can watch and learn from in its entirety.
Next, let's briefly cover Amaro's rewards. When you kill Amaro, you'll get her head, as well as 30 to 40 level five
ascension shards. She also has a one in 10 chance of dropping a serrated claw, which you can use to craft the level
five scimitar, Amaro's Talon. But chances are you won't get that. We need to simply time to go turn in Amaro's
head to Death and collect your bag of rewards. When you go back to Death at the entrance of Fell Hollow and give him
Amaro's head, he'll give you the Withering Heights reward pack, which includes the Tome of the Undying, the
Undead Draconic Visage, and the Dragon Curse Shield. You can use the Undead Draconic Visage to make a Dragon Curse
Shield if you need another one, and it's also an ingredient in Amaro's Talon. The Tome of the Undying gives you 750
experience, and attack, ranged, and magic. So, a pretty decent boost. And from there, it's simply time to move on
to the next stage of your journey, which is traveling to Douwdan Reach. You do so by talking to the ghost of
Cathen, who's at the end of this path near Silverthorn Keep. When you're doing the part of the main quest that involves

comments.author: @skyknighteman7022
comments.text:
After eight successful kills I finally managed to get the recipe for Imaru's Talon. I went with ranged since that's what I'd been using throughout the story. My gear was the Green Dragonhide ranged armor set, the Steel Crossbow and the Hunter Stagbow. I always go with both a crossbow and a longbow because that gives me more flexibility in battle. With the crossbow I used Enchanted Steel Bolts because they have a chance to drain a bit of health from the enemies and heal a bit for me. The ammo that I used for the longbow was Barbed Steel Arrows. I also brought Egg Royale (Salmon + fried egg) for the Sea Life buff, Fish Fry (fried cabbage, Lobster and Undead Eel) because it heals 180 health at a time and only gives 55 sustenance, and Evasive infusion for the drink.

In each battle I'd start with the longbow to get some quick early damage off while things are still not too chaotic. When Imaru flies up to do her Wither Ball shot attack I would be able to get off one or two aimed shots at her core, which is her weak point. Once adds start showing up I would switch to the crossbow, take them out quickly, and then just keep firing at the boss and getting off what damage I can. I never really prioritized getting soul rifted when she turned into her ghost form since I'm never able to get a lot of shots off in that state and I often ended up making mistakes and jumping off the edge while trying to get purified and avoid taking too much damage. The only time I would soul rift was in the final stage of the fight since once Imaru dies you instantly return to normal and all the adds die with her, so at that point I'd just rush to her and try to end the fight as soon as possible.

With patience and luck I was eventually able to get the drop I was aiming for and I am now starting to make my way into Dowdun Reach. May you rest peacefully for all eternity Imaru.
